established_findings.statement: Research demonstrates active application of LLMs to intent-driven network management and automated translation of natural-language intents into low-level network configurations (prototypes, benchmarks, and production-threaded frameworks reported).
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical and system papers / framework reports
limitations: Varies across papers between prototype, testbed, and claimed production; implementations and evaluation breadth differ.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented architectures (LLMs calling external tools, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-tool agents) are a prominent pattern to improve grounding, factuality, and task automation in domain workflows including NetOps analogues.
established_findings.evidence_type: system papers, focused studies, and surveys
limitations: Most evidence is cross-domain (statistics, chemistry, drilling) or survey-level; direct NetOps-only empirical comparisons are fewer.

established_findings.statement: A substantial literature emphasizes hallucination, constraint violations, and unreliable factuality in LLM outputs and proposes detection/mitigation (entropy-based detectors, constrained decoding, consistency/self-verification).
limitations: Mitigation methods reduce but do not eliminate failures; many evaluations are on general-language or other-domain benchmarks rather than large-scale NetOps deployments.

established_findings.statement: Security, governance, and runtime-authorization architectures (protocol-mediated execution, runtime authorization/twin simulation, execution-witness binding) are proposed as necessary guardrails for agentic systems acting on infrastructure.
established_findings.evidence_type: architectural and prototype defense papers / surveys
limitations: Prototypes show promise under modeled conditions; robustness under real-world sensor/state mismatch and adversarial adaptation varies between studies.

established_findings.statement: Benchmarks and evaluation suites for LLMs in networking and security contexts exist (NetConfEval, CyberMetric, AIOpsArena, specialized honeypot LLM benchmarking), but vary in scope and evaluation axes.
limitations: Benchmarks focus on different tasks (QA, configuration translation, microservices AIOps, honeypot realism), lacking a single unified safety/verification NetOps benchmark.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent LLM-driven intent-to-configuration pipelines produce operationally safe, deployment-grade network changes across diverse vendors and live production states remains insufficiently empirically characterized.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: mixed (prototype claims and surveys pointing to limited external validation)
limitations: Some frameworks report production use (e.g., Confucius) but independent, large-scale cross-vendor replication and failure-rate reporting are limited in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well verifier/authorization layers (twins, protocol-mediated governance) maintain safety under realistic measurement noise, state mismatch, and adversarial/indirect prompt-injection in NetOps settings needs more systematic quantification.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: prototype evaluation papers and security attack study
limitations: Some papers examine model-mismatch scenarios but full-spectrum adversarial robustness evaluations in NetOps are sparse in these records.

unresolved_questions.statement: There is limited consensus or standardization on metrics that jointly capture functional correctness, safety (policy compliance), and risk (blast radius) for generated network changes.
limitations: Multiple proposals exist but no single, widely-adopted metric suite appears in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: The comparative effectiveness of constrained-generation decoding (e.g., IPCD) versus post-hoc verification+repair workflows for preventing harmful NetOps actions is not settled in the supplied literature.
limitations: IPCD and related constrained-decoding methods are evaluated in non-NetOps domains in the supplied records; direct NetOps head-to-head comparisons are not present.

candidate_gaps.statement: A unified, safety-focused NetOps benchmark that evaluates end-to-end generate→verify→authorize→apply pipelines (including measurement noise, vendor heterogeneity, and adversarial data injections) is not evident in the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: gap inference from benchmark and survey literature
limitations: Existing benchmarks cover parts of the pipeline; absence claim limited to supplied records only.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies measuring real-world failure modes (frequency, root causes, and operational impact) of LLM-generated network configurations under production-like perturbations are scarce in the supplied set.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: inferred from prototypes and surveys lacking extensive failure-data
limitations: Some authors report operational experience but systematic, quantified failure-mode datasets are not prominent in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Standardized evaluation metrics that integrate security threat models (indirect prompt injection, tool misuse) with NetOps correctness metrics are underdeveloped in the supplied literature.
limitations: Security taxonomies exist, but their combination with operational NetOps correctness benchmarks is not evident in these records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Comparative evaluations of constrained-decoding (hard-constraint generation) versus external verifier-first architectures specifically on network-configuration synthesis tasks are missing from the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: method papers and surveys indicating methodological divergence
limitations: Constrained-decoding work is present but assessed mainly outside NetOps; direct comparative NetOps studies are not supplied.

excluded_claims: LLMs are ready to operate unguarded as autonomous NetOps agents in production without external verification or governance (no supplied record provides unqualified empirical support).
Any single architectural pattern (e.g., tool-augmented agents) universally eliminates hallucination or unsafe outputs across NetOps (unsupported by supplied empirical evidence).
There is conclusive evidence that constrained decoding alone guarantees production-grade safety for network configuration generation (no supplied NetOps-specific proof).
